summary: Jakob Steiner studied at Heidelberg University (1818–1821) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1822–1824). He held posts at Beuth Hochschule für Technik Berlin (1825–1834) and Frederick William University Berlin (1834–1863).

Indologist and religious studies scholar Jakob Wilhelm Hauer studied at Basel Mission, Oxford, and Tübingen (Ph.D., Habilitation) under Richard von Garbe. He served as Privatdozent (1919) and chairholder (1927–1945) at Tübingen, and professor of Indology at Marburg (1925–1927).

Jakub Čejka, a scholar of Indology and Tibetology, studied at Charles University, completing an MA (1990–1998) and a BA (2018). He was affiliated with Savitribai Phule Pune University, attested in 1996–1997.
Active in Buddhist studies, Jambugahapitiye Dhammaloka studied under Clemency Montelle and held a post at the University of Canterbury circa 2013–2017.

James A. Benn, specializing in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, studied at Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held posts at Lewis & Clark College and McMaster University, where he became professor.

James A. Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held posts at California State University as Professor of Religion (attested 1998) and at California State University, Fullerton as Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion (attested 2007).
James Adam studied at the University of Aberdeen (circa 1876–1880) and Gonville and Caius College (circa 1880–1884), working in philosophy and related fields.

Linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist James Alan Matisoff studied at Harvard, International Christian University, and UC Berkeley (Ph.D. 1967). He taught at Columbia University (1966–1969) and was a professor at UC Berkeley from 1970 to 2002.

James Atkinson, a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology, studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the Indian Medical Service, Fort William College (Assistant Persian Professor, 1818), and the India Government Mint, Kolkata.

Scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology James B. Apple earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he studied under doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne alongside numerous other academic and traditional teachers.

James Bird studied at the University of Aberdeen (M.A. 1810–1814) and Guy's and St Thomas'. Active in Indology and archaeology, he served as assistant surgeon in Bombay Presidency (1818) and secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (1844–1847).

James Bissett Pratt studied at Williams College, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Harvard (Ph.D. under William James). He was a professor of philosophy at Williams College (1905, 1917–1943) and taught at Visva-Bharati University (1931–1932).

James Blumenthal studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD under Geshe Lhundup Sopa) and Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. He held faculty posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College, specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology.
James Bradstreet Greenough, an Indologist and linguist, earned his A.B. at Harvard University (1852–1856) and served there as Tutor of Latin from 1865 to 1873.

James Burgess studied at the universities of Glasgow and Edinburgh. An Indologist and archaeologist, he served at Doveton College, the Bombay Geographical Society, and the Archaeological Survey of India, where he was Director General from 1886 to 1889.

James Burnell Robinson studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and advisor Geshe Lhundup Sopa. A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, he was an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa (attested 1996).
James Burnes was an Indology and history scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh and received an LL.D. from the University of Glasgow by 1834.

James C. Dobbins, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, earned his PhD from Yale University by 1984 and served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015–2019).

James C. Harle studied at Princeton (B.A.) and Oxford (B.A., D.Phil., D.Litt.). In Indology and archaeology, he worked at Princeton (1947–1949) and the Ashmolean Museum as Assistant Keeper (1960) and Keeper (1967–1987).

Indologist James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland studied at East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck. He served as Registrar at Calcutta High Court (1810), Principal of Hooghly Mohsin College (1839), and law professor at Presidency University.
